question: In a logic circuit, three SPST (Single Pole Single Throw) switches are used to implement a logic gate. The switches are connected in series. What is the output of the circuit if all switches are closed?

options.text: The output will depend on the type of gate used

solution:
The correct answer is __1**(1)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The circuit uses three SPST switches connected in series.
 
• When all switches are closed, the circuit is completed, and the output is 1.
 
• SPST switches are simple on/off switches, and their state determines the circuit’s output.
 
• If any of the switches are open, the circuit will not be completed, resulting in an output of 0.
 
• In this case, since all switches are closed, the circuit is completed, and the output is 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SPST Switch:**

 
 
• SPST stands for Single Pole Single Throw.
 
• It is a basic switch used to either connect or disconnect a circuit.
 
 
 
• **Series Connection:**
 
 
• In a series connection, all components are connected end-to-end.
 
• If one component is open or faulty, the entire circuit is disrupted.
 
 
 
• **Logic Circuit Output:**
 
 
• The output depends on the configuration and state of the switches.
 
• For this scenario, the output is 1 when all switches are closed.
